_: WHAT MAY APPEAR IN A PUBLIC REPOSITORY, stated as SHAPES.
This is an ALLOWLIST and it is never inverted. A list of forbidden strings
would have to spell out the hostnames, addresses and identifiers it exists
to keep out of a public tree — publishing them in the guard itself — and it
would catch only what somebody had already thought of. Everything here is a
shape that is SAFE to publish, and the guard reports anything else.
Nothing in this file names a person, a private host or a real identifier.
That property is the point of the file and is worth checking on every edit.
Read by .github/scripts/publication-guard.py.
skipPaths: _comment: binaries, vendored trees and lockfiles. DECLARED here rather than hardcoded, so widening the scan is an edit to data.

_: A candidate is a dotted name whose last label is a TLD below, or a name
reached through a scheme, or a cluster-internal suffix. Everything else
is not treated as a host at all — which is why a source filename never
becomes a finding.
ignoredLastLabels: _comment: extensions that collide with a TLD. A filename is not a host.
allowed: _comment: RESERVED EXAMPLE SPACE — RFC 2606 and RFC 6761.
_comment: CLUSTER-INTERNAL. Meaningless outside a cluster, so it identifies nothing.
_comment: THIS PROJECT, and the forge it is published from.
_comment: THE OTHER PUBLIC FORGES, so the repository rule can name where it applies.
_comment: KUBERNETES API GROUPS. Not hosts at all — they wear the shape.
_comment: TOOLCHAIN, VENDOR AND STANDARDS HOSTS this repository legitimately names.

_: Loopback, the unspecified address, and the ranges RFC 5737 and RFC 3849
reserve for documentation. A private-range literal is NOT allowed by its
range — a 10.x address names somebody's cluster.
CLONE and REMOTE urls only — a bare module path in a go.mod is a
dependency, not a deployment, and a registry path is not a repository.
So the rule applies to the FORGES below plus any url ending `.git`, and
the one repository this project may name in a clone url is itself.
allowed: _comment: UPSTREAM PROJECTS the documentation links. A public project is not a private deployment, and each is declared so the list stays readable as what it is.

_: Chat, group and thread identifiers. ONE placeholder is documented, and
every example carries it. A second VALUE is a real surface — the two
entries below are one value in the two spellings the transport itself
produces, signed and deep-link.
The rule is scoped to where such an identifier LIVES — a field whose
NAME says so, a transport url that carries one in its path, or the
signed form a supergroup id takes. Scoping by CONTEXT rather than by
digit count is what keeps a timestamp or a cursor in a test fixture
from reading as a surface, and it names no value anywhere.
allowed: _comment: THE documented placeholder, and the same value with its supergroup prefix removed — the form a deep link carries. One placeholder, two spellings the transport itself produces.

email._: Addresses at the reserved example domains, plus the forge's own no-reply.
allowedDomains: _comment: the co-author trailer every commit in this repository carries.
